newsitem.title: USA: Rover Sojourner deployed, rolls onto Mars surface.
newsitem.headline: Rover Sojourner deployed, rolls onto Mars surface.

text.p: The Mars rover rolled down a ramp from the Pathfinder space lander late on Saturday onto the surface of the "Red Planet", U.S. space officials said.
The six-wheeled buggy-type vehicle named "Sojourner" was scheduled to begin exploring the surface of Mars on Sunday, analysing its rocks and soil for at least one week.

The successful deployment came after a day of suspense at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory here where space officials had feared the scientific aspects of the $266-million mission might be hurt by a communications glitch.
However, communications between the lander and Sojourner were later restored, allowing signals from mission control to get through to the rover's on-board computer.

After a ramp was lowered, the rover was told to "stand-up" from its stowed position and once the wheel bogeys were locked in place, the tiny 22-pound (10 kg) vehicle -- looking like a workbench or microwave oven on wheels -- slowly moved down the 35-degree slope onto the Martian surface. Officials confirmed at 10.59 p.m. PDT (0559GMT Sunday) that the rover was on the planet's surface.

During its exploration, the solar-powered rover will navigate with the aid of laser beams, will take 3-D photographs with its twin-lens camera and will be able to pick up and analyze samples of rocks and soil and transmit the data to Earth.
